types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman, Actor. Examples: Brenda Fricker, Phil Belfield, Christy Brown, Daniel Day-Lewis.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Person' directly matches schema.org's 'Person', which describes an individual human being, fitting all mentions.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Film: A motion picture or movie, typically produced for cinematic release or television broadcast. Also called Movie, Picture, Motion Picture, Feature Film. Examples: My Left Foot, Home Alone 2, A Time to Kill, So I Married an Axe Murderer.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Film' directly matches schema.org's 'Movie', which is a creative work that is a motion picture film, fitting all examples.

mentions: So I Married an Axe Murderer

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or honor bestowed for achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Accolade, Trophy. Examples: Academy Award, Oscar.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: A prize or honor bestowed for achievement.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents an 'Award' as an entity; existing candidates are events or actions. Minting 'Award' as a new type under 'Thing' is the best fit.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A specific calendar year. Also called Annual period, Calendar year, Annum. Examples: 1989, 1986, 1992, 2003.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's 'Date' is a datatype for a full date, and 'Duration' is a quantity for a length of time, neither precisely matching a specific calendar year as an entity. Minting 'CalendarYear' under 'Thing' is more appropriate.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Fictional Character Role: The part played by an actor in a fictional work. Also called Acting role, Character portrayal, Part. Examples: Pigeon Lady.

chosen_type.label: PerformanceRole
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Fictional Character Role' directly matches schema.org's 'PerformanceRole', which describes a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, fitting the example 'Pigeon Lady'.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

types.embedding_query_text: News Organization: An entity responsible for gathering and disseminating news and information. Also called Media outlet, News agency, Broadcaster, Publisher. Examples: CBS News, BBC, The Guardian newspaper, The Guardian.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'News Organization' directly matches schema.org's 'NewsMediaOrganization', which describes organizations that produce and disseminate news, fitting all mentions.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A specific day within a calendar week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day, Date. Examples: Friday, Thursday night.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'DayOfWeek' directly matches schema.org's 'DayOfWeek', an enumeration for specific days of the week, fitting all mentions.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center, Municipality. Examples: Dublin, London, New York City, Big Apple.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'City' directly matches schema.org's 'City', which describes a large human settlement and administrative area, fitting all mentions.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

types.embedding_query_text: Television Series: A sequence of television programs with a common title or theme, usually presented in installments. Also called TV show, Series, Program, Show. Examples: Casualty.

chosen_type.label: TVSeries
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Television Series' directly matches schema.org's 'TVSeries', which describes a creative work series for television broadcast, fitting the mention 'Casualty'.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Award Category: A specific division or classification within an award system. Also called Prize category, Award division, Recognition class. Examples: best supporting actress, best actor.

chosen_type.label: CategoryCode
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's 'CategoryCode' describes a specific code within a classification system, which accurately represents an 'Award Category' like 'best supporting actress'.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: Rating
candidates.comment: A Rating is an Intangible representing an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars. Also called score, grade, review rating. Examples: a 4-star movie rating, a product's 8/10 score, a customer satisfaction rating of 5 out of 5, a restaurant's health inspection grade.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

types.embedding_query_text: Medical Condition: A state of health that deviates from the normal, often requiring medical attention. Also called Illness, Disease, Ailment, Disorder. Examples: cerebral palsy.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Medical Condition' directly matches schema.org's 'MedicalCondition', which describes any condition affecting normal body functioning, fitting 'cerebral palsy'.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalCause
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".

types.embedding_query_text: Fictional Character: An imaginary person or entity in a literary or dramatic work. Also called Character, Persona, Role. Examples: Brown's mother, Kevin.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's 'Person' explicitly includes fictional individuals, making it a perfect match for 'Fictional Character' and the given examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: ComicStory
candidates.comment: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state occupying a particular territory. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm. Examples: Ireland.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Country' directly matches schema.org's 'Country', which describes a sovereign state or nation, fitting 'Ireland'.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.embedding_query_text: Park: An area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or for the protection of wildlife or natural habitats. Also called Garden, Green space, Recreational area. Examples: Central Park.

chosen_type.label: Park
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Park' directly matches schema.org's 'Park', which describes an area set aside for recreation or wildlife, fitting 'Central Park'.

candidates.label: Park
candidates.comment: A Park is a civic structure or area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or protection of wildlife. Also called public park, green space, recreation area. Examples: Central Park in New York City, a local neighborhood park, a national park. Distinct from Garden, which is typically smaller and privately owned.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: Playground
candidates.comment: A Playground is a CivicStructure designed for children's recreational play. Also called play area, recreation ground. Examples: a school playground, a park playground, an indoor play center, a community playground.

candidates.label: RVPark
candidates.comment: An RVPark is a CivicStructure offering space for recreational vehicles, caravans, or mobile homes. Also called RV campground, caravan park, motorhome park. Examples: "KOA Campground", a state park RV site, a private RV resort, a mobile home park.

candidates.label: Cemetery
candidates.comment: A civic structure designated as a burial ground for the deceased. Also called graveyard, burial ground, memorial park, necropolis. Examples: Arlington National Cemetery, Père Lachaise Cemetery, a local municipal cemetery.

types.embedding_query_text: Decade: A period of ten years. Also called Ten-year period, Ten years. Examples: 1990s.

chosen_type.label: Decade
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate specifically represents a calendar decade as an entity; 'Duration' is too generic. Minting 'Decade' under 'Thing' is the most precise option.

candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. candidates.label: Duration

types.embedding_query_text: Book: A written or printed work consisting of pages bound together, typically published as a single volume. Also called Publication, Volume, Text, Work. Examples: She Died Young: A Life in Fragments, memoir, autobiography.

chosen_type.label: Book
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Book' directly matches schema.org's 'Book', which describes a written or printed work, fitting the example title.

mentions: She Died Young: A Life in Fragments

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: BookFormatType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing the physical or digital publication format of a book. Also called book edition type, publication format, reading format. Examples: "Hardcover", "Paperback", "Ebook", "Audiobook".

types.embedding_query_text: Social Issue: A problem that influences a considerable number of individuals within a society. Also called Societal problem, Public concern, Community issue. Examples: sexual violence.

chosen_type.label: SocialIssue
chosen_type.definition: A problem that influences a considerable number of individuals within a society.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate adequately represents a 'Social Issue' as an abstract problem. Minting 'SocialIssue' under 'Thing' is the best fit.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
candidates.comment: HealthAspectEnumeration is an enumeration of various aspects of health content, used to describe specific facets of health topics online. Also called health content categories, medical information facets, wellness topic types. Examples: 'Symptoms', 'Treatments', 'Causes', 'Prevention'.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: PublicToilet
candidates.comment: A PublicToilet is a CivicStructure containing one or more toilets available for use by the general public, customers, or employees. Also called public restroom, public convenience, washroom. Examples: a toilet in a park, a restroom in a shopping mall, a public toilet facility at a train station, a highway rest stop bathroom.

types.embedding_query_text: Life Stage: A distinct period in the life cycle of an individual, characterized by specific developmental tasks or social roles. Also called Phase of life, Developmental stage, Period of life. Examples: teenager.

chosen_type.label: LifeStage
chosen_type.definition: A distinct period in the life cycle of an individual, characterized by specific developmental tasks or social roles.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a 'Life Stage' like 'teenager'. Existing candidates are for media seasons or schedules. Minting 'LifeStage' under 'Thing' is the best fit.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification. Also called Occupation, Career, Vocation, Job. Examples: career, psychiatrists.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Profession' directly matches schema.org's 'Occupation', which describes a profession involving training and qualification, fitting 'career' and 'psychiatrists'.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Physician
candidates.comment: A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor. Examples: a general practitioner, a specialist physician, a family doctor's clinic. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger medical facility.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.
